viral_tweets.title_en:
🤖 Remember when Anthropic ran a 26B AI model across fifteen $55 Android TV boxes?

📱Someone is turning old Android phones into Local AI clusters. 

And they're running GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B-A3B across just TWO phones.

This open-source project is called PhoneBorg.

Here are the developer's reported distributed inference benchmarks ...

🧠 GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 (12.1GB)
📱 2 phones → 2.6–2.8 tps
🧠 Qwen3-30B-A3B Q3 (13.8GB)
📱 2 phones → 2.57 tps
📱 5 phones → 1.66 tps

🧠 Qwen3-32B Q4_K_M (19.8GB)
📱 4 phones → 0.89 tps
📱 5 phones → 0.75 tps

The developer's five-phone cluster consists of ...
📱 Google Pixel 8 Pro → 12GB
📱 OnePlus 10 Pro → 12GB
📱 POCO F3 → 8GB
📱 Xiaomi Mi 8 → 6GB
📱 Xiaomi Mi 9 → 6GB

That's 44GB of combined RAM.

On November 21, the developer added Android TV-box support.

A 2017 NVIDIA Shield TV with just 3GB RAM is running ...
⚡ LFM2-350M → 17.9 tps
⚡ Qwen2.5-0.5B → 10.3 tps

PhoneBorg can also ...
✅ Distribute a large model across multiple phones
✅ Process multiple independent requests in parallel
✅ Divide tasks among AI agents
✅ Route requests to different models
✅ Expose an OpenAI-compatible API
✅ Integrate with coding agents via MCP

Built on llama.cpp.
Apache 2.0 license.

It's still a proof of concept, and adding more phones increases available memory but can actually reduce single-stream inference speed.

The developer even references Anthropic's $55 TV-box experiment.

How many of us have old Android phones sitting in a drawer doing absolutely nothing?

Maybe it's time to put them back to work. 🔥

GitHub in ALT.

viral_tweets.quote_zh:
🤖 还记得 Anthropic 在 15 个 55 美元的 Android 电视盒上运行 26B AI 模型吗？

📱有人正在将旧的 Android 手机变成本地 AI 集群。

他们仅在两部手机上运行 GPT-OSS-20B 和 Qwen3-30B-A3B。

这个开源项目称为 PhoneBorg。

以下是开发人员报告的分布式推理基准......

🧠 GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 (12.1GB)
📱 2 部手机 → 2.6–2.8 tps
🧠Qwen3-30B-A3B Q3（13.8GB）
📱 2 部手机 → 2.57 tps
📱 5 部手机 → 1.66 tps

🧠Qwen3-32B Q4_K_M (19.8GB)
📱 4 部手机 → 0.89 tps
📱 5 部手机 → 0.75 tps

开发人员的五部手机集群包括...
📱 谷歌 Pixel 8 Pro → 12GB
📱 OnePlus 10 Pro → 12GB
📱 POCO F3 → 8GB
📱 小米 8 → 6GB
📱 小米 9 → 6GB

这就是 44GB 的组合 RAM。

11 月 21 日，开发者添加了 Android 电视盒支持。

一台只有 3GB RAM 的 2017 款 NVIDIA Shield TV 正在运行......
⚡ LFM2-350M → 17.9 吨/秒
⚡ Qwen2.5-0.5B → 10.3 tps

PhoneBorg还可以...
✅ 在多部手机上分发大型模型
✅ 并行处理多个独立请求
✅ 在 AI 代理之间分配任务
✅ 将请求路由到不同的模型
✅ 公开 OpenAI 兼容的 API
✅ 通过 MCP 与编码代理集成

基于 llama.cpp 构建。
阿帕奇 2.0 许可证。

它仍然是一个概念证明，添加更多手机会增加可用内存，但实际上会降低单流推理速度。

开发者甚至参考了 Anthropic 的 55 美元电视盒实验。

我们中有多少人的抽屉里放着旧的 Android 手机，什么都不做？

也许是时候让他们重返工作岗位了。 🔥

GitHub 中的 ALT。

💰 ~$1,000 on sale

✅ Lemonade

top_three.summary_en: Mathematician Terence Tao suggests AI is shifting mathematical research toward an industrial 'Big Math' collaboration model. While acknowledging AI's potential in mapping large-scale problems, he criticizes current LLM proofs as 'toxic waste' due to their lack of underlying logic, interpretability, and rigor.
paragraphs: Renowned mathematician Terence Tao expects AI to overhaul how his field is organized. On the Hard Fork podcast, he calls this "Big Math,"paralleling the decades-old "Big Science"model. Mathematicians will collaborate in ever larger groups, he says, with even postdocs and PhD students leading ambitious projects because AI speeds up entry into complex topics. Human-AI teams could systematically map thousands of problems rather than solving them individually. Tao described a similar "industrialization of mathematics"in 2024.

Still, he sharply criticizes current AI results from major tech companies. The models solve open problems and contribute technically, he says, but produce answers without understanding and can't explain their proofs. Such proofs are "toxic waste"to those companies, in his view: an unwanted byproduct of training better models that firms must dump after minimal cleanup. In October, Tao and other mathematicians called for an OpenAI boycott.

He's equally critical of AI-generated papers flooding academic journals. They sometimes solve open problems, he says, but often fail to open new research directions, cite sloppily, explain poorly, and aren't enjoyable to read. Eventually, Tao hopes AI will deliver the "first awful solution,"and humans will structure it properly and put it into clear context.

paragraphs: Stay ahead with our breaking stories and exclusive coverage prioritized on Google.

Jensen Huang’s reported resignation as NVIDIA chief executive in November 2026 marked a dramatic turn in the career of the man who helped build the company into one of the world’s most valuable technology businesses. His departure followed reports concerning his personal relationships, questions about his professional associations and an investigation by the company’s board.

Huang’s journey from a difficult childhood in Taiwan to the leadership of a global semiconductor giant reflects decades of ambition, business setbacks and technological achievements. Under his leadership, NVIDIA became a central player in the artificial intelligence industry, reaching a valuation of $5 trillion in October 2025. However, the latest developments surrounding his personal life and corporate position have brought a different dimension to his legacy.

Born in Tainan, Taiwan, in 1963, Huang moved to the United States at the age of nine with his older brother. Their parents sent them to live with an uncle, who believed he had arranged places for them at a good boarding school in Kentucky. The institution, however, turned out to be a reform school.

Huang reportedly spent part of his daily routine cleaning toilets. His roommate was a 17-year-old with knife scars from fights. The two developed an unusual friendship. Huang taught him to read, while his roommate introduced him to weightlifting. Huang also developed his table tennis skills and became nationally ranked as a teenager.

His family later reunited in Oregon, where Huang worked as a dishwasher and busboy at Denny’s while attending high school. He skipped two grades and graduated at 16. In 1984, he earned an electrical engineering degree from Oregon State University. His laboratory partner was Lori, whom he later married.
Huang subsequently worked at AMD and LSI Logic before completing a master’s degree at Stanford University in 1992 while continuing to work full time.

While working in the technology industry, Huang began meeting engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem at a Denny’s restaurant in San Jose. Their discussions eventually led to the establishment of NVIDIA in 1993, when Huang was 30.

The company’s early years were marked by commercial difficulties. Its first chip, the NV1, failed in 1995. A subsequent chip developed for Sega’s next gaming console also failed to meet expectations. Huang informed Sega that NVIDIA could not deliver the product but asked the company to invest in the business regardless.

Sega reportedly invested $5 million, which Huang later described as all the money the company had. Facing serious financial pressure, he reduced NVIDIA’s workforce from approximately 100 employees to 40. For several years, he reportedly opened meetings by telling employees that the company was 30 days away from going out of business.

The situation improved in 1997 when NVIDIA’s RIVA 128 chip sold one million units within its first four months. The company went public in 1999 at $12 a share and introduced the GeForce 256, which it described as the world’s first GPU. Microsoft subsequently selected NVIDIA to develop the graphics chip for its first Xbox console.

top_three.summary_en: Reddit COO Jen Wong addressed recent stock volatility and traffic risks posed by AI-driven search, emphasizing the platform's long-term value through high user stickiness across life stages. Despite declines in search referrals, Reddit intends to navigate the shift via strategic partnerships with search engines and by leveraging its unique repository of long-tenured user engagement.
paragraphs: Reddit boasts engagement metrics that would be the envy of many other online platforms: Over 80% of its monetization comes from loyal, logged-in users, who spend eight times as much time on the site in their fifth year as they did in their first.And yet, Reddit’s share price is down 62% for the year to date, as the platform grapples with an internet increasingly shaped by AI.In its Q3 earnings call in October, Reddit’s CEO, Steve Huffman, said Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode were leading to a decline in search referrals to the site, the lifeblood of many social and media-adjacent businesses. The market did not like the implications, and the share price dropped from just shy of $130 apiece to a little under $91 overnight.

Chief Operating Officer Jen Wong told Fortune in an exclusive interview that some factors were lost in translation. The shifting relationship between Reddit and search engines “requires a different kind of partnership,” she said, rather than any separation. If anything, Wong believes Reddit is well-positioned to navigate the new era of online information gathering.

In their first year on Reddit, users tend to spend five minutes a day on the app or website. By their fifth year, that figure rises to 40 minutes, Wong tells Fortune. The number of “communities” (topic-focused discussion groups) that users are in jumps from 10 in the first year to more than 100 by their fifth.

“Reddit is really interesting because we have users who have over a decade of karma,” Wong said. “Reddit typically gets you as a young adult, and then you season over time in this incredible way. If you look at the chart, it’s very consistent.”

Wong sees users’ changing life stages reflected in the communities they join: “[They’ve] gone through life with Reddit. You started as a student, you got your first rental place, you got married, you had kids, and we see kind of your life’s journey.
“You just never age out of Reddit because all of those life stages are available to you on Reddit, and you’re always going through something that you have to traverse.”

Navigating different life stages appears to be a key differentiator of the Reddit platform. In 2024, an article published in “Higher Education Research and Development” found that one in three students use Reddit for study help, ahead of TikTok at 14.9% and Instagram at 12.7%. YouTube leads the pack, with more than 90% of the 1,000 students surveyed using it for educational purposes.
The site’s leadership wants to expand on that function. In early November, Reddit launched Reddit Reviews, organizing product feedback across multiple communities to provide overall ratings.

“Logged-in users season very, very well, which is another motivation for us to say we want more logged-in users, because we want the opportunity to teach you about all these other aspects of Reddit,” Wong adds, “Not just the information and retrieval part of Reddit, but the part of Reddit that is around the connection, the communities, and the conversation.”

Every media platform needs to maintain or grow its audience. But Reddit has a unique problem: It has more than 100,000 “communities,” according to various reports, all of which have volunteer moderators. These moderators are unpaid and are not Reddit employees, instead choosing to spend their free time building their communities and ensuring the content is fit for its purpose.
But with ever-evolving channels and new voices within them, demand for experienced moderators is high—in fact, Reddit even has a dedicated page where communities can recruit volunteer moderators.

In the recruitment group, individuals are either looking for or offering moderation skills for hours a day, on a daily basis. Posts include requests for moderators in specific time zones, often for about 3 hours a day.

linked_tweets.author: @edwinarbus
linked_tweets.content_zh:
克劳德没有受过破坏工作的训练。是的，它有时会犯错误，其他特工可能会识别出错误，但这不是破坏。

有一些过时的《神鬼寓言 5》系统卡的屏幕截图。在 6 月份《神鬼寓言 5》发布的前两天，我们确实对一些法学硕士研究应用了不可见的保护措施。这是一个错误，我们于 6 月 10 日逆转了它。这些保护措施现在明确阻止请求或回退，并显示用户可以看到的消息 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback)。

我们确实训练了《神鬼寓言 5.2》使其具有与 Opus 5.5 水平相当的 LLM 研究能力，并在发布时如此表示 (https://anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2)。这会影响能力，但不会默默地破坏工作。

据我们所知，一些报告看起来像是我们所说的模型行为中的“过度谨慎”，即克劳德在长时间运行的任务中过度依赖它为自己制定的规则。这并不是机器学习研究所特有的，我们在没有这些训练变化的模型（包括 Opus 5.5）以及我们自己的工作中也看到了这一点。您可以要求克劳德审查并删除它为自己制定的规则，我们正在努力减少未来模型中的过度谨慎。我们不会故意干扰用户的工作。

我们已直接回复此处要求提供会话 ID 的大量报告，但请分享（运行“/status”）！
linked_tweets.content_en:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

linked_tweets.content_zh:
Leopold Aschenbrenner 解释了下一个三年人工智能贸易的投资方向

他在第三季度的投资者信中表示，市场低估了人工智能从聊天机器人到代理再到超级智能的速度

他预计 2027 年将把 3 年的人工智能进展压缩为 1 年

他的信主要围绕这些公司/股票：

• 基础模型：人择是主要选择，因为模型本身就成为了产品。 Situational Awareness LP (SALP) 表示，Anthropic ARR 在 22 个月内增长了约 80 倍，从约 $1B 增长到约 $81B，并认为领先的人工智能实验室可能会以 1T+ 的综合收入运行率退出 2027 年

• 内存芯片供应：如果长期运行的人工智能代理使内存和存储变得更有价值，SK Hynix、Kioxia 和 SanDisk 就会受益。 Leopold 表示，强化学习和代理使 AI 芯片受到内存的限制，这就是为什么他认为 Hynix 是一家 100B 美元的公司，可能会成为一家 1T 美元的公司

• GPU 租赁：如果人工智能实验室继续以更高的价格租赁短期 GPU 容量，SpaceX、Nebius、SharonAI、CoreWeave 和 IREN 就会受益。 SALP 表示，H100 过去每小时收入约为 1-2 美元，现在每小时收入约为 5-10 美元，如果超级智能需求达到，每小时可能会达到 100 美元以上

• 数据中心电源：如果人工智能数据中心支付更多费用以更快地获得电力，Bloom Energy 就会受益。人工智能建设需要的不仅仅是廉价电力，它还需要立即电力

• 机器人技术：如果人工智能开始从事现实世界的劳动，机器人技术将成为下一个主题。利奥波德表示，前沿模型开始击败专业机器人模型，这意味着下一个进步可能来自更好的人工智能模型

利奥波德警告说，一旦人工智能能够取代他们所重视的工程师、代码、IP和管理，软件公司、人工智能包装商、芯片设计师，甚至今天的人工智能获胜者都可能会失去护城河

linked_tweets.content_en:
Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade

His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence

He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 year

his letter focuses around these companies/stocks:

• Foundation Models: Anthropic is the main bet because the model itself becomes the product. Situational Awareness LP (SALP) says Anthropic ARR grew ~80x in 22 months, from ~$1B to ~$81B, and argues leading AI labs could exit 2027 at $1T+ combined revenue run-rate

• Memory Chip Supply: SK Hynix, Kioxia, and SanDisk benefit if long-running AI agents make memory and storage more valuable. Leopold says reinforcement learning and agents make AI chips limited by memory, which is why he viewed Hynix as a $100B company that could become a $1T company

• GPU Rentals: SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, and IREN benefit if AI labs keep renting short-term GPU capacity at higher prices. SALP says an H100 used to earn ~$1-$2/hour, now earns ~$5-$10/hour, and could reach $100s/hour+ if superintelligence demand hits

• Datacenter Power Supply: Bloom Energy benefits if AI datacenters pay more to get power online faster. AI buildout needs more than cheap power, it needs power immediately 

• Robotics: Robotics becomes the next major theme if AI starts doing real-world labor. Leopold says frontier models are starting to beat specialist robotics models, which means the next advancement may come from better AI models

Leopold warns software companies, AI wrappers, chip designers, and even today’s AI winners may lose their moats once AI can replace the engineers, code, IP, and management they are valued on

linked_tweets.author: @amitisinvesting
linked_tweets.content_zh:
我已经读了大约 30 页的第三季度态势感知信函。整封信有160页。

到目前为止我能说的是，如果利奥波德对人工智能发展方向的看法是正确的……整个人工智能堆栈的市场估值与我们预期的增长水平之间的脱节是我们在金融市场上见过的最大脱节之一。

其中一些预测相当令人难以置信，但我想这也是他的基金的意义所在。他写道：“无论是我们还是市场，一年内都会出现大量的鸡蛋。”

明天读完整篇文章后，我将发表更深入的想法，迄今为止最有趣的见解：他认为前沿实验室将在 2027 年底前完成 1T 美元的 ARR，机器人技术的 ChatGPT 时刻将在 2027 年底到来，而 RSI 正在被市场大幅打折，最终可能变得如此强劲，以至于可能导致政府关闭所有模型。

我们正生活在投资者最疯狂的时代之一。
linked_tweets.content_en:
I am about 30 pages into the Q3 Situational Awareness letter. The full letter is 160 pages.

All I can say so far is that if Leopold is right about where he sees AI going...the disconnect between market valuations across the AI stack and the level of growth we should expect is one of the largest disconnects we have ever seen in financial markets.

Some of these predictions are quite hard to believe, but I guess that's also the point of his fund. He writes, "Either we or the market will have an extraordinary amount of egg on the face in a year."

Will post deeper thoughts tomorrow after reading through the whole thing, the most interesting insights so far: he thinks the frontier labs will do $1T of ARR by end of 2027, a ChatGPT moment for Robotics will come by late 2027, and that RSI is significantly being discounted by the market which could end up becoming so strong that it could lead to the shutdown of all models by the government.

We are living in one of the craziest times to be an investor.

news.title: Terence Tao sees AI ushering in "Big Math,"but calls major tech firms' proofs "toxic waste"
news.title_en: Terence Tao sees AI ushering in "Big Math,"but calls major tech firms' proofs "toxic waste"
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet: Renowned mathematician Terence Tao expects AI to overhaul how his field is organized. On the Hard Fork podcast, he calls this "Big Math,"paralleling the decades-old "Big Science"model. Mathematicians will collaborate in ever larger groups, he says, with even postdocs and PhD students leading ambitious projects because AI speeds up entry into complex topics. Human-AI teams could systematically map thousands of problems rather than solving them individually. Tao described a similar "industrializat
news.summary_en: Mathematician Terence Tao suggests AI is shifting mathematical research toward an industrial 'Big Math' collaboration model. While acknowledging AI's potential in mapping large-scale problems, he criticizes current LLM proofs as 'toxic waste' due to their lack of underlying logic, interpretability, and rigor.
paragraphs: Renowned mathematician Terence Tao expects AI to overhaul how his field is organized. On the Hard Fork podcast, he calls this "Big Math,"paralleling the decades-old "Big Science"model. Mathematicians will collaborate in ever larger groups, he says, with even postdocs and PhD students leading ambitious projects because AI speeds up entry into complex topics. Human-AI teams could systematically map thousands of problems rather than solving them individually. Tao described a similar "industrialization of mathematics"in 2024.

Still, he sharply criticizes current AI results from major tech companies. The models solve open problems and contribute technically, he says, but produce answers without understanding and can't explain their proofs. Such proofs are "toxic waste"to those companies, in his view: an unwanted byproduct of training better models that firms must dump after minimal cleanup. In October, Tao and other mathematicians called for an OpenAI boycott.

He's equally critical of AI-generated papers flooding academic journals. They sometimes solve open problems, he says, but often fail to open new research directions, cite sloppily, explain poorly, and aren't enjoyable to read. Eventually, Tao hopes AI will deliver the "first awful solution,"and humans will structure it properly and put it into clear context.

news.summary_en: Liam Byrne, Chair of the UK House of Commons Business Committee, has formally requested Pip White, Anthropic's head of UK and Ireland, to provide the unredacted version of the November 5 METR safety report by December 4. The committee is probing the internal acceleration of AI development and the rationale behind Anthropic’s decision to redact critical evidence from the assessment.
paragraphs: The UK Parliament wants Anthropic to hand over the unredacted version of an AI safety report. Liam Byrne, who chairs the House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, made the request in a letter dated November 27. It went to Pip White, Anthropic's head of UK and Ireland. Byrne wants a complete, unredacted copy of METR's November 5 report on how fast AI research and development at Anthropic was accelerating in October.

METR, an AI safety organization, has said publicly that Anthropic cut major parts of the report before publication, including much of the evidence the group called "most informative."Byrne, whose inquiry centers on AI safety, wants the redacted material by December 4, along with an explanation of why it was redacted.

METR's report described a substantial risk that AI development at Anthropic could speed up further by a factor of 1.3 to 3, and the group found no clear bottlenecks. METR says the public has to rely on the evaluators' judgment more than would be ideal because Anthropic redacted most of the evidence.

fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Industry Leaders: Power operators are using sensors and software to dynamically adjust grid safety limits, boosting existing network capacity amid rising AI-driven energy demand (Martha Muir/Financial Times)
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Operators are using sensors and sophisticated software to eke out more capacity from installed transmission lines as they struggle ….
[Key Metrics] In contrast, accommodating an extra 330GW of generation, storage and demand by expanding the grid would cost around $100bn.
paragraphs: The wind has long been harnessed to generate electricity. Now, with the advent of new technologies, a breezy day gives engineers the opportunity to increase the capacity of the grid to deliver more power where it is needed.

Utilities have traditionally placed hard limits on how much power can flow through their wires to prevent damaging them. But the development of a suite of sensors and sophisticated software that tracks local climatic conditions is allowing engineers to predict the cooling effect of the wind on the cables — as the temperature of a metallic conductor drops, so does its electrical resistance — allowing them to raise the safety limit to pump more power through the grid.

This process, known as dynamic line rating, is one of a number of “grid-enhancing” technologies that hold out the promise of increasing the capacity of existing networks. Other innovations include software that redirects power away from congested transmission lines, sensors to identify spare capacity across the grid and controls to balance supply and demand in real time.

Squeezing more out of installed transmission lines is key for grid operators as they struggle to deal with an increasingly urgent mismatch between supply and demand for power, as the world moves into what the International Energy Agency has dubbed the “age of electricity”. Global electricity demand is forecast to grow 3.6 per cent annually through to 2030, 50 per cent faster than the average rate over the past decade, according to the IEA.

Installing new electricity-generating capacity takes time — power plants and transmission lines can take more than a decade to build — but data centres can spring up in a few years. The rising demand, which is being driven by AI, industrial electrification, electric vehicles, heat pumps and air conditioning, has put utilities under pressure to find faster, cheaper ways to try to address the mismatch without spending billions of dollars on infrastructure.

In Britain, National Grid is using dynamic line rating on 900km of its network, which is expected to increase capacity by 8 per cent. The company says it has already saved customers more than £21mn over the past five years by reducing the costs of managing congestion on its electricity network.

In Norway, the grid operator Statnett has installed sensors on a transmission line built in the 1950s, estimating the technology could boost capacity by up to 30 per cent. “It gives us the opportunity to get more out of old lines,” says Halvor Lund, a senior analyst at Statnett.
In the US, utility PPL spent $1mn installing sensors across 31 miles of transmission lines in Pennsylvania, which meant it could scrap a $12mn project to replace existing cables.

As well as the financial savings, the potential to increase the capacity of existing infrastructure is substantial. The IEA estimates that dynamic line ratings and other grid technologies could unlock capacity for 330 gigawatts globally of generation, storage and demand, equivalent to roughly 3 per cent of the world’s capacity. In contrast, accommodating an extra 330GW of generation, storage and demand by expanding the grid would cost around $100bn.

Freeing up 0.5 per cent of peak demand at a utility serving 1mn customers would provide enough electricity to connect a new data centre to the grid rather than have to spend years building a new power plant, explains Peter Mainz, chief executive at Landis+Gyr, the Swiss grid technology group. “I know that in three years, you’re not going to have a nuclear power plant up and running,” he adds. “So I think technology can do much more.”

Other technologies can be used to change how electricity moves through the grid. Power controllers — devices which include long-established mechanical transformers and newer automated electronics — redirect electricity to underused transmission routes, while separate software can identify alternative routes to bypass congested lines.

This article is part of a report called Business of Energy, highlighting some of the issues facing nuclear, electricity grids, the oil and gas industry and solar and wind generation. Read the rest of the report here

news.title: Robotics startup Embo raises $110 million in seed funding to build world-model AI for robots
news.title_en: Robotics startup Embo raises $110 million in seed funding to build world-model AI for robots
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
Robotics AI startup Embo has raised $110 million in seed funding to build AI models for smarter everyday robots. Andreessen Horowitz led the round, joined by Khosla Ventures, DST Global, and Nvidia, Embo says. Its unified model pretrains on large amounts of internet video as a world model that learns how objects and physical interactions work. The AI then practices motor skills in simulated scenarios before fine-tuning on experience from a humanoid robot fleet.

The team says it worked on Dreame
news.summary_en: Robotics AI startup Embo announced a $110 million seed funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Nvidia, Khosla Ventures, and DST Global. The company focuses on developing 'world models' pretrained on massive internet video datasets, employing reinforcement learning in simulations followed by fine-tuning on humanoid robot fleets to overcome generalization hurdles in physical interactions.
paragraphs: Robotics AI startup Embo has raised $110 million in seed funding to build AI models for smarter everyday robots. Andreessen Horowitz led the round, joined by Khosla Ventures, DST Global, and Nvidia, Embo says. Its unified model pretrains on large amounts of internet video as a world model that learns how objects and physical interactions work. The AI then practices motor skills in simulated scenarios before fine-tuning on experience from a humanoid robot fleet.

The team says it worked on Dreamer, VideoGPT, and Diffusion Forcing and brings experience from Google Deepmind, Meta Superintelligence Labs, Nvidia Cosmos, UC Berkeley, and MIT. Today's robots often fail in unfamiliar situations. Embo says it's countering that by training a model from scratch with reinforcement learning.

Embo isn't alone. In robotics, world action models are seen as the next paradigm, where world models feed imagined future frames into a pretrained robotics AI. Stanford professor Fei-Fei Li founded World Labs in 2024 and raised $230 million for spatial intelligence, also backed by Andreessen Horowitz and Nvidia. Our Frontier Radar #5 deep dive covers the new AI labs and their bets, including World Labs, which will soon operate under AMD.

paragraphs: Stay ahead with our breaking stories and exclusive coverage prioritized on Google.

Jensen Huang’s reported resignation as NVIDIA chief executive in November 2026 marked a dramatic turn in the career of the man who helped build the company into one of the world’s most valuable technology businesses. His departure followed reports concerning his personal relationships, questions about his professional associations and an investigation by the company’s board.

Huang’s journey from a difficult childhood in Taiwan to the leadership of a global semiconductor giant reflects decades of ambition, business setbacks and technological achievements. Under his leadership, NVIDIA became a central player in the artificial intelligence industry, reaching a valuation of $5 trillion in October 2025. However, the latest developments surrounding his personal life and corporate position have brought a different dimension to his legacy.

Born in Tainan, Taiwan, in 1963, Huang moved to the United States at the age of nine with his older brother. Their parents sent them to live with an uncle, who believed he had arranged places for them at a good boarding school in Kentucky. The institution, however, turned out to be a reform school.

Huang reportedly spent part of his daily routine cleaning toilets. His roommate was a 17-year-old with knife scars from fights. The two developed an unusual friendship. Huang taught him to read, while his roommate introduced him to weightlifting. Huang also developed his table tennis skills and became nationally ranked as a teenager.

His family later reunited in Oregon, where Huang worked as a dishwasher and busboy at Denny’s while attending high school. He skipped two grades and graduated at 16. In 1984, he earned an electrical engineering degree from Oregon State University. His laboratory partner was Lori, whom he later married.
Huang subsequently worked at AMD and LSI Logic before completing a master’s degree at Stanford University in 1992 while continuing to work full time.

While working in the technology industry, Huang began meeting engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem at a Denny’s restaurant in San Jose. Their discussions eventually led to the establishment of NVIDIA in 1993, when Huang was 30.

The company’s early years were marked by commercial difficulties. Its first chip, the NV1, failed in 1995. A subsequent chip developed for Sega’s next gaming console also failed to meet expectations. Huang informed Sega that NVIDIA could not deliver the product but asked the company to invest in the business regardless.

Sega reportedly invested $5 million, which Huang later described as all the money the company had. Facing serious financial pressure, he reduced NVIDIA’s workforce from approximately 100 employees to 40. For several years, he reportedly opened meetings by telling employees that the company was 30 days away from going out of business.

The situation improved in 1997 when NVIDIA’s RIVA 128 chip sold one million units within its first four months. The company went public in 1999 at $12 a share and introduced the GeForce 256, which it described as the world’s first GPU. Microsoft subsequently selected NVIDIA to develop the graphics chip for its first Xbox console.

paragraphs_zh: Swedish fintech Trustly today confirmed it had completed a $60m funding round, having last month said it had received $40m in commitments from its key shareholders.

Trustly said it had received a total of $60m from its main shareholder, Nordic Capital, and Alfvén & Didrikson, another existing shareholder, while other existing shareholders, including funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, participated in the capital raise.

Trustly said the funds will be used to speed up the development of new AI-powered products. Trustly, which has raised over $450m in funding, leverages open banking technology to allow its customers to pay directly from their bank account without needing to use a card or app.

It is an alternative payment method to card giants Visa and MasterCard. In September this year, Trustly said it was cutting around 200 jobs, around a quarter of its overall headcount, after it saw its revenues fall by more than $50m last year.

Johan Tjärnberg, Group CEO of Trustly, said: “The capital raised will accelerate the development of new products that leverage AI to turn payments into intelligence, helping businesses win new customers, retain them for longer and stay ahead of risk.
Trustly is building on its leading open banking payments network across the US, Canada and Europe to create a real-time intelligence platform, so that each interaction becomes smarter than the last.”

news.author: Eleanor Pringle
news.content_snippet: Reddit boasts engagement metrics that would be the envy of many other online platforms: Over 80% of its monetization comes from loyal, logged-in users, who spend eight times as much time on the site in their fifth year as they did in their first.And yet, Reddit’s share price is down 62% for the year to date, as the platform grapples with an internet increasingly shaped by AI.In its Q3 earnings call in October, Reddit’s CEO, Steve Huffman, said Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode were leading to a
news.summary_en: Reddit COO Jen Wong addressed recent stock volatility and traffic risks posed by AI-driven search, emphasizing the platform's long-term value through high user stickiness across life stages. Despite declines in search referrals, Reddit intends to navigate the shift via strategic partnerships with search engines and by leveraging its unique repository of long-tenured user engagement.
paragraphs: Reddit boasts engagement metrics that would be the envy of many other online platforms: Over 80% of its monetization comes from loyal, logged-in users, who spend eight times as much time on the site in their fifth year as they did in their first.And yet, Reddit’s share price is down 62% for the year to date, as the platform grapples with an internet increasingly shaped by AI.In its Q3 earnings call in October, Reddit’s CEO, Steve Huffman, said Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode were leading to a decline in search referrals to the site, the lifeblood of many social and media-adjacent businesses. The market did not like the implications, and the share price dropped from just shy of $130 apiece to a little under $91 overnight.

Chief Operating Officer Jen Wong told Fortune in an exclusive interview that some factors were lost in translation. The shifting relationship between Reddit and search engines “requires a different kind of partnership,” she said, rather than any separation. If anything, Wong believes Reddit is well-positioned to navigate the new era of online information gathering.

In their first year on Reddit, users tend to spend five minutes a day on the app or website. By their fifth year, that figure rises to 40 minutes, Wong tells Fortune. The number of “communities” (topic-focused discussion groups) that users are in jumps from 10 in the first year to more than 100 by their fifth.

“Reddit is really interesting because we have users who have over a decade of karma,” Wong said. “Reddit typically gets you as a young adult, and then you season over time in this incredible way. If you look at the chart, it’s very consistent.”

Wong sees users’ changing life stages reflected in the communities they join: “[They’ve] gone through life with Reddit. You started as a student, you got your first rental place, you got married, you had kids, and we see kind of your life’s journey.
“You just never age out of Reddit because all of those life stages are available to you on Reddit, and you’re always going through something that you have to traverse.”

Navigating different life stages appears to be a key differentiator of the Reddit platform. In 2024, an article published in “Higher Education Research and Development” found that one in three students use Reddit for study help, ahead of TikTok at 14.9% and Instagram at 12.7%. YouTube leads the pack, with more than 90% of the 1,000 students surveyed using it for educational purposes.
The site’s leadership wants to expand on that function. In early November, Reddit launched Reddit Reviews, organizing product feedback across multiple communities to provide overall ratings.

“Logged-in users season very, very well, which is another motivation for us to say we want more logged-in users, because we want the opportunity to teach you about all these other aspects of Reddit,” Wong adds, “Not just the information and retrieval part of Reddit, but the part of Reddit that is around the connection, the communities, and the conversation.”

Every media platform needs to maintain or grow its audience. But Reddit has a unique problem: It has more than 100,000 “communities,” according to various reports, all of which have volunteer moderators. These moderators are unpaid and are not Reddit employees, instead choosing to spend their free time building their communities and ensuring the content is fit for its purpose.
But with ever-evolving channels and new voices within them, demand for experienced moderators is high—in fact, Reddit even has a dedicated page where communities can recruit volunteer moderators.

In the recruitment group, individuals are either looking for or offering moderation skills for hours a day, on a daily basis. Posts include requests for moderators in specific time zones, often for about 3 hours a day.

news.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and alleged coercion of shared suppliers
news.title_en: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and alleged coercion of shared suppliers
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
OpenAI is suing Apple for trade secret theft and unfair business practices. The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit Friday in a California court, the Financial Times reports. OpenAI accuses Apple of "coercing and threatening"suppliers that work with both companies and of using its market power to stifle competition.

The company also alleges that Apple encourages employees to store corporate data on personal devices, then turns that practice against staff who want to leave. According to the complain
news.summary_en: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple in a California court, accusing the company of unfair business practices, including coercing shared suppliers and abusing its market power. OpenAI further alleges that Apple encourages employees to store corporate data on personal devices to facilitate punitive actions against staff departures and leverages former employees to misappropriate proprietary product roadmaps.
paragraphs: OpenAI is suing Apple for trade secret theft and unfair business practices. The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit Friday in a California court, the Financial Times reports. OpenAI accuses Apple of "coercing and threatening"suppliers that work with both companies and of using its market power to stifle competition.

The company also alleges that Apple encourages employees to store corporate data on personal devices, then turns that practice against staff who want to leave. According to the complaint, a former OpenAI employee passed along details about product plans and suppliers after returning to Apple.

The countersuit follows Apple's own lawsuit from the summer, which accused several former employees of leaking confidential information to OpenAI. The AI company had previously closed its $6.4 billion acquisition of former Apple chief designer Jony Ive's studio "io"and is preparing its own devices to rival Apple. Just two years ago, the two companies made a splashy announcement of a partnership to integrate ChatGPT into the iPhone.

news.summary_en: OpenAI filed a countersuit in a California court accusing Apple of leveraging its supply chain dominance to coerce suppliers and block collaboration with the AI firm. This follows Apple's prior legal claims alleging that former employees, including OpenAI's Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan, misappropriated sensitive product and supply chain data, marking a direct escalation of the rivalry into the AI-native hardware space.
paragraphs: OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, in an effort to “compete unfairly by any means available”.
The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, striking back after the iPhone maker accused the AI lab of stealing top-secret information this summer.
The escalating legal battle will further sour the relationship between the two Silicon Valley companies, which just two years ago struck a partnership to embed ChatGPT into the iPhone.
The new legal action comes after OpenAI acquired io, the studio led by Apple’s former design chief Sir Jony Ive, for $6.4bn in May last year.
The AI company is preparing to launch a range of new personal devices that it says could “outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf”.

OpenAI claims that Apple is using its “size and wealth to forestall competition”, including threatening suppliers that might work on its new devices, alleging a “wide variety of unlawful, unfair, and tortious conduct”.
Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The iPhone maker has long used its supply chain might to its advantage, paying upfront to lock in capacity of key components or manufacturing resources to ensure its products have the latest chips.
But OpenAI accused Apple of going further by “coercing and threatening” suppliers that are also working with the ChatGPT maker.
OpenAI also said that one of its former employees who returned to Apple shared details about its product plans and suppliers.

Apple in July accused several of its former employees, including OpenAI’s chief hardware officer Tang Tan, of sharing confidential information with their new employer about Apple’s product development and supply chain.
Another former Apple engineer exploited a “vulnerability” in Apple’s network storage to steal confidential files after he left the company, the iPhone maker claimed.

news.title: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
news.title_en: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
news.author: Oliver Barnes, Sujeet Indap, and Kieran Smith
news.content_snippet:
US telecoms company Verizon is in talks over a roughly $6bn deal to buy fibre-optic broadband operator Fidium in a potential boost to its goal of making its network available to as many as 50mn homes and businesses nationwide.

The potential acquisition would come on the heels of the completion of Verizon’s $20bn takeover of Frontier Communications earlier this year, which added 2.2mn fibre-optic subscribers across 25 US states and expanded its network to reach an additional 9mn premises.

Offer
news.summary_en: Verizon is in advanced talks to acquire fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium for approximately $6 billion. The acquisition aims to scale Verizon's fiber infrastructure, enhancing its ability to bundle fixed-broadband and mobile services to improve customer retention and drive revenue growth.
paragraphs: US telecoms company Verizon is in talks over a roughly $6bn deal to buy fibre-optic broadband operator Fidium in a potential boost to its goal of making its network available to as many as 50mn homes and businesses nationwide.

The potential acquisition would come on the heels of the completion of Verizon’s $20bn takeover of Frontier Communications earlier this year, which added 2.2mn fibre-optic subscribers across 25 US states and expanded its network to reach an additional 9mn premises.

Offering bundles of high-speed home internet and mobile coverage has been a growth priority for Verizon to reduce customer churn and boost revenues per customer. Shares in the group are up more than 17 per cent this year, giving it a market capitalisation of $198bn as the company has been aggressively investing to build out its US fibre-optic network.

Discussions between Verizon and Fidium’s owners — midmarket private equity group Searchlight Capital Partners and Canadian fund manager British Columbia Investment Management Corporation — are ongoing, according to people familiar with the matter.

The potential deal, which could value Illinois-based Fidium at about $6bn including debt, may be agreed in the coming weeks, the people said. They added it is possible another bidder could emerge and there are no guarantees the talks will result in a deal. Searchlight and BCI bought Fidium, then known as Consolidated Communications, in a $3.1bn take-private deal in 2024.
Verizon and Searchlight declined to comment. BCI and Fidium did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Fidium operates in 21 states, including California and Texas, but would strengthen Verizon’s presence in northern New England by adding a subscriber base of 351,000 homes across states including Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont. Fidium is aiming to make its fibre-optic network available to up to 2mn homes nationwide by the end of 2027, rising from 1.5mn at present.

Verizon chief executive Dan Schulman at the start of the year cited “a possibility of both inorganic and partnerships” to boost its fibre-optic network reach. Schulman said the company expects such a network to be accessible to 32mn premises by year-end as part of its medium-term goal to grow the network to between 40mn and 50mn fibre connections.

Even as Verizon’s shares have rallied this year, mobile operators are girding for the chance that Elon Musk’s SpaceX may soon enter the consumer wireless industry. In a recent podcast with Fortune Magazine, Schulman said SpaceX would need to spend more than $300bn over several years to reach the scale of Verizon.

news.title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
news.title_en: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
It's no surprise at this point, but for the record: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia's powerful Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The details come from documents filed with Chinese regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg.

According to the filings, Shanghai Shuoyao offered a GB300-NVL72 rack as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, while a second company, Shanghai Kezhan
news.summary_en: Shanghai Shuoyao and Shanghai Kezhan listed Nvidia GB300-NVL72 racks and GB200 servers as loan collateral in filings with Shanghai Innovation Bank. The hardware traces back to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte, and Shanghai Shuoyao maintains deep business ties with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm recently added to the US trade blacklist.
paragraphs: It's no surprise at this point, but for the record: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia's powerful Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The details come from documents filed with Chinese regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg.

According to the filings, Shanghai Shuoyao offered a GB300-NVL72 rack as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, while a second company, Shanghai Kezhan, listed a GB200 server at the same site in loan documents. Exporting these chips to China without a US license is banned. Bloomberg traced the rack to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte through a serial number in a public warranty database.

Shanghai Shuoyao is closely tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed, according to Bloomberg. The Trump administration added Megaspeed to a US trade blacklist this month on suspicion of chip smuggling. Alice Huang founded Megaspeed in 2023, and Nvidia approved it as a partner within four days. It went on to become Nvidia's largest customer in Southeast Asia, Bloomberg reported.
The newly tightened US export rules and anti-diffusion measures are reportedly already causing headaches for Chinese AI startups.

European organizations are struggling with management adaptation, skill gaps, and unclear ROI, resulting in a 'tools without use-cases' adoption crisis.
paragraphs: Europe is falling behind the US on AI use at work, and the main reason is not technology, according to a new report.The report from Sifted, sponsored by London Business School, says Europe has an organisational gap rather than a tech gap. Firms struggle with skills, management, trust and the cost of fitting AI into how they work.
“Doing a fun thing with ChatGPT and running your whole business on AI are two very different things,” Celonis executive Rupal Karia told Sifted.

About 43% of US workers used AI for their jobs in early 2026, against 32% across Europe, a St Louis Fed analysis found. US workers spent more than three times as many work hours using AI as those in Germany, France and Italy.
Only 20% of EU firms use AI at all, up from 13.5% a year earlier, Eurostat data shows. Denmark leads at 42%, while Romania sits at 5.2%.
Even where firms use AI, few have gone all in. The report cites McKinsey data showing 88% of organisations use AI somewhere, but just 7% have fully scaled it.
“There is no inherent roadblock to Europe leading in AI adoption,” said Nicos Savva, a professor at London Business School.

Karia, who runs northern Europe and the Middle East for German software firm Celonis, said many companies had underestimated the human side of change. Adoption has been slower than expected, he added.

Executives cited unreliable outputs, cyber risk and running costs as reasons for caution. Some firms are now limiting AI use as they weigh cost against benefit, LBS deputy dean Gary Dushnitsky told Sifted.
Returns are also hard to find. The report cites research from marketing firm Whito showing 75% of firms using AI see productivity gains, but only 12% see more revenue.
Paul Maker, technology chief at UK firm Aiimi, put it bluntly.
“Everyone’s been given a hammer and now they’re desperately looking for nails,” he said.
Fear of job losses is also slowing take-up, said LBS professor Lynda Gratton.

news.content_snippet:

news.summary_en: AI scientist Yann LeCun left Meta in late 2025 to co-found AMI Labs. paragraphs: AI pioneer Yann LeCun doesn't believe language models alone will lead to human-like intelligence. With his JEPA architecture, he is pursuing machines that model cause and effect and plan their actions in advance. Three new studies show how the pieces of this project fit together and where physics still sets limits.

In late 2025, Yann LeCun left Meta after shaping its AI research for 12 years. He cited the company's growing focus on large language models as one reason, then co-founded the Paris startup AMI Labs and raised more than $1 billion. While much of the tech industry trains increasingly large chatbots, LeCun is focusing on systems for robotics, industry, and wearable devices intended to operate in the physical world.

news.title_en: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform, report says
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.content_snippet:
Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud platform. Reuters reports that attackers penetrated Cloud One, the Air Force's central cloud infrastructure, potentially exposing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data. The breach was discovered last month during routine system upgrades.

According to one source, the attackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain access to the platform's control plane. Cloud One has pooled cloud resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alp
news.summary_en: The US Air Force's Cloud One platform has been breached by hackers who exploited a software vulnerability to infiltrate the control plane, potentially exposing sensitive air defense and logistics data. The Air Force has responded by blocking updates, revoking admin privileges, and engaging US Cyber Command to assess the breach impact.
paragraphs: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud platform. Reuters reports that attackers penetrated Cloud One, the Air Force's central cloud infrastructure, potentially exposing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data. The breach was discovered last month during routine system upgrades.

According to one source, the attackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain access to the platform's control plane. Cloud One has pooled cloud resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet since 2017, running applications that include air defense radar and munitions management. In response, the Air Force paused migration of additional applications, blocked updates, and revoked administrator privileges. US Cyber Command is assessing the damage.

The breach comes amid growing concern about AI-powered attacks, as AI models can rapidly identify vulnerabilities across large cloud networks. At least six other cyber incidents have hit US government agencies recently, and Microsoft's cybersecurity division reported widespread use of the AI tool ARTEX. Who carried out the attack and whether any data was exfiltrated remain unknown.

news.title: OpenAI is building "Athena"data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
news.title_en: OpenAI is building "Athena"data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
OpenAI is building a data management platform codenamed "Athena"to make its AI agents more accurate when working with business data. Athena resembles a semantic layer, software that provides consistent definitions for business metrics such as revenue and customer count, The Information reports.

The report says at least one customer found that ChatGPT Work's data analysis agent, launched last fall, wasn't accurate enough. The idea is to give agents the context they need so they guess less. A per
news.summary_en: OpenAI is developing a data platform codenamed 'Athena' to create a semantic layer for consistent business metrics, aimed at reducing AI agents' reliance on guesswork during data analysis. The initiative addresses accuracy concerns in current AI tools and serves as a strategic move to deepen enterprise software integration.
paragraphs: OpenAI is building a data management platform codenamed "Athena"to make its AI agents more accurate when working with business data. Athena resembles a semantic layer, software that provides consistent definitions for business metrics such as revenue and customer count, The Information reports.

The report says at least one customer found that ChatGPT Work's data analysis agent, launched last fall, wasn't accurate enough. The idea is to give agents the context they need so they guess less. A person familiar with the plans says OpenAI is using Athena to build agents that collect, document, and update business rules, so other agents don't have to start from scratch every time. Data platforms such as Snowflake and Databricks already offer their own semantic layers.

Athena could be an effort to build a stronger competitive advantage, since the report says it's harder to switch semantic layer providers than to switch AI models. The platform is still in early development, and OpenAI hasn't shared a timeline or pricing.

news.title: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
news.title_en: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.summary_en:
Days after GTA 6's record console launch, numerous projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build to PC. AI coding agents are dramatically speeding up reverse engineering and shaking up Rockstar's business model.

A core pillar of Rockstar's business strategy is under pressure just days after Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale. The game had a historic debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S with an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day revenue. But a day later, the hacking group CyberLeek dis
paragraphs: Days after GTA 6's record console launch, numerous projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build to PC. AI coding agents are dramatically speeding up reverse engineering and shaking up Rockstar's business model.

A core pillar of Rockstar's business strategy is under pressure just days after Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale. The game had a historic debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S with an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day revenue. But a day later, the hacking group CyberLeek distributed a stolen Xbox image of the game, and the executable itself leaked a few days ago.

Since then, a fast-moving scene of developers and modders has sprung up to get the game running on Windows through reverse engineering, compatibility layers, and recompilation. AI coding tools like Anthropic's Claude Code are driving that pace. Instead of spending months manually analyzing code and rebuilding console functions, developers are handing off much of the porting work to AI agents. One group even livestreamed the process.
### One GTA 6 PC port passes 90 percent progress as early multiplayer surfaces within days

A tracking platform lists 40 active projects less than four days after the executable leaked. Nearly half of them can boot the game on PC. On the platform's own rating scale, the furthest project is more than 90 percent of the way to a playable PC build.

Some projects are trying to add features including native ray-traced lighting. Gameplay footage of an unofficial PC multiplayer mode surfaced on November 26, and the platform's operator verified it. It shows multiple players moving through the game world with vehicles and voice chat at 25 to 30 frames per second. GTA 6 has officially launched only as a single-player title, and an online mode has no release date yet.

There is no finished PC version ready for the general public yet. The most stable builds are incomplete, circulate in closed groups, or require substantial technical know-how. Even so, this pace breaks a decades-old assumption in the gaming industry. Console emulators often took years after a hardware generation launched, and brand-new blockbusters rarely ran on them soon after release.
### Unofficial PC ports threaten Rockstar's delayed launches and online business

Rockstar and parent company Take-Two face more than a technical nuisance. The studio traditionally releases its flagship games on consoles first and follows with PC versions much later. GTA V took about 19 months to reach PC, and Red Dead Redemption 2 took about a year. So far, there is no official PC release date for GTA 6. That approach cuts optimization work at launch and encourages impatient players to buy the game twice.

The online business is an even bigger vulnerability. Nearly 80 percent of Take-Two's total revenue in fiscal year 2026 came from microtransactions and recurring digital spending. GTA Online alone has brought in more than $5 billion so far. A free, community-run PC multiplayer mode targets that financial backbone before Rockstar has even launched its own version.

Past experience with FiveM for GTA V shows how nervous Take-Two is about parallel worlds like this. In 2015, the company cracked down hard on the alternative multiplayer and roleplay mod. It banned developer accounts and, according to some developers, even sent private investigators to the creators' homes to shut down the project.

FiveM grew into the core of the roleplay scene despite that pushback and at times drew more concurrent players on Steam than the base game. Only then did Rockstar reverse course and acquire the development team Cfx.re in August 2023. Back then, the community needed years to build a parallel ecosystem like that. For GTA 6, an early PC multiplayer prototype has surfaced just a week after launch.

paragraphs: SAP is preparing to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as part of a sweeping AI restructuring, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. That's at least nine percent of the company's global workforce of more than 110,000. Every department has been asked to identify savings, with product development, engineering, and sales taking the biggest hit. The final number hasn't been set and could change after negotiations with employee representatives.

In Germany, where about a quarter of SAP's workforce is based, a job guarantee runs through 2028. CEO Christian Klein wants to embed AI tools across SAP's product lineup. The company already cut roughly 10,000 jobs in 2024. Its competitors are making similar moves. Oracle slashed 21,000 positions over twelve months, and Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees. SAP declined to comment on the potential cuts, saying only that it reviews its organizational structure on an ongoing basis. The company recently announced a partnership with Mistral AI and has acquired several startups.

news.content_snippet:
At Huawei Technologies’ headquarters in Shenzhen, China, a palatial corridor gleams with gold ceilings and elaborate frescoes of Russian aristocrats on galloping horses. It bears the name of the American president who tried to bring the Chinese technology giant to its knees.

Huawei executives call it the “Trump Corridor,” a pointed reference to President Trump’s campaign during his first term to drive the company out of global wireless networks and cut off its access to advanced chips.

The nam
news.summary_en: Facing prolonged US export controls and recent federal court verdicts regarding trade secret theft and sanctions evasion, Huawei is intensifying its R&D into high-performance AI chips. Under Ren Zhengfei's leadership, the company has consolidated its identity as the core of China's technological autonomy, positioning its silicon as the primary domestic alternative to Nvidia amid tightening semiconductor access.
paragraphs: At Huawei Technologies’ headquarters in Shenzhen, China, a palatial corridor gleams with gold ceilings and elaborate frescoes of Russian aristocrats on galloping horses. It bears the name of the American president who tried to bring the Chinese technology giant to its knees.

Huawei executives call it the “Trump Corridor,” a pointed reference to President Trump’s campaign during his first term to drive the company out of global wireless networks and cut off its access to advanced chips.

The name is a gesture of defiance. Having survived punishing American sanctions, Huawei is determined to prove that Washington cannot dictate its future. That resolve faces a new test after the company was convicted this week in an American court of stealing trade secrets.

In 2019, Mr. Trump’s crackdown threatened Huawei’s survival, just as it had become a world leader in telecommunications and consumer devices. Seven years later, Huawei is central to Beijing’s ambitions to challenge the United States in artificial intelligence. Its chips are the closest thing China has to an answer to Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.

Last month, in a vaulted conference room beyond the corridor, Ren Zhengfei, Huawei’s 82-year-old founder and chief executive, credited the American president with forcing Huawei and China into a new era of self-reliance.
“Pass on our thanks to him, and also share the story of the Trump Corridor as well,” Mr. Ren said in an interview.
After the U.S. crackdown, he said, Huawei cemented its identity as “a company of our own country.”

Huawei’s resurgence illustrates a paradox in Washington’s efforts to contain China’s technological rise. The company was among the first targets of export restrictions that became a policy blueprint. American restrictions have slowed China’s advances, but they have also galvanized a national effort to dismantle the technological dependencies that gave Washington leverage.

On Tuesday, after an 11-week trial, a federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets from American companies and evading sanctions against Iran. Huawei said the verdicts were “without legal or factual merit.”

As its American ties unravel, Huawei is becoming more indispensable to China. This month, the Trump administration announced plans to block Chinese companies from accessing advanced A.I. chips through overseas data centers, closing one of the last routes to Nvidia’s most powerful semiconductors.

The move comes amid turmoil at Nvidia. Jensen Huang, its chief executive, resigned two weeks ago following allegations of an affair with an executive at the Singaporean data center company Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence officials believe the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with a Chinese Ministry of State Security officer during their relationship. Beijing has denied spying.

This week, Mr. Huang returned as chief executive after a pressure campaign by President Trump, who said the reversal was necessary to ensure the “success and prosperity” of Nvidia and the American economy.

news.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
news.title_en: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
news.author: Allison Johnson
news.content_snippet:
Aside from dealing with my calendar, there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus.

What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking u
news.summary_en: Google has rolled out the beta version of 'Create My Widget' for Pixel devices. Integrated into the Gemini Intelligence suite, the feature enables users to generate custom home screen widgets via natural language prompts, aiming to enhance AI utility in direct operating system interactions.
paragraphs: Aside from dealing with my calendar, there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus.

What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.

I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.

I also made a widget that will display the words “Tut tut, looks like rain” whenever it’s raining. This is silly, and it accomplishes nothing except making me happy. I couldn’t think of anything clever it should say when there’s no rain, so it just says “No rain right now” otherwise. But I live in Seattle, so I’ll get a lot of mileage out of this widget.

The create-a-widget interface suggests a few ideas and categories, leaning on more practical uses like habit trackers and recipe inspiration. Fine, I’ll try something normal, I thought. I’m trying to get better about my daily mental health walk, so I had it make a widget for logging a week’s worth of walks. I was hoping for something visual that would trick my little monkey brain into keeping a streak going. Instead, I got something simply labeled “Log Walk” that triggers Gemini to add a walk to my calendar when I tap it. At least Gemini suggested the extra step of creating a checklist where I could mark off the days of the week as I completed my little walk.

It took me a minute to get my head around it, but many of the widgets are basically little prompt shortcuts for Gemini. You tap one, it pulls up the Gemini interface on your home screen, thinks for a while, then comes up with whatever you were asking for. The kinds of widgets you can make also seem to fit into some well-defined templates. You can create a widget that displays a countdown to a holiday or certain event on your calendar. You can show a recent score and upcoming game time for your favorite sports team. For anything more open ended, your widget will pull from Google search results (suggest a different three-ingredient cocktail recipe every day, for example) or prompt Gemini to figure it out for you. I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature. Fair, I guess.
"I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature"

That’s why my bus schedule widget didn’t really work out. I asked for a list of real-time arrivals; it gave me a tile that reads “Bus Arrivals” and uses Gemini to search for arrival times for the stop I specified. Gemini is helpful for some things but useless for this; it gives me a wordy response about how often the bus runs and when I might expect it to arrive based on the schedule. Not what I had in mind. On the bright side, my Jurassic Park quote widget had some words of wisdom for me: “Life, uh, finds a way.” That’ll do for now.

Bloomberg News is finding that some of Nvidia's Blackwell chips did turn up at these Chinese sites linked to Megaspeed. Tyler Kendall, thank you so much uh as always for that reporting. Matt Bloxham of Bloomberg Intelligence joins us now with more. news.content_snippet:
Chinese food-delivery giant Meituan reported a second consecutive profitable quarter on Friday, as the company navigates intensifying competition from Alibaba Group Holding and JD.com while seeking to sustain its earnings recovery.

The Beijing-based firm’s adjusted net profit for the three months ended September came in at 1.9 billion yuan (US$285.1 million), slightly missing analysts’ expectations of 2.2 billion yuan, marking a second straight quarterly profit after the company returned to the
news.summary_en: Meituan reported total revenue of 115.6 billion yuan for Q3, up 21.6% YoY, exceeding analyst estimates, with an adjusted net profit of 1.9 billion yuan, marking two consecutive quarters of profitability. CEO Wang Xing and CFO Chen Shaohui attributed this performance to enhanced operational efficiency and a more rational competitive landscape, shifting strategic focus toward long-term value in the instant retail ecosystem.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade

His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence

He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 year

his letter focuses around these companies/stocks:

• Foundation Models: Anthropic is the main bet because the model itself becomes the product. Situational Awareness LP (SALP) says Anthropic ARR grew ~80x in 22 months, from ~$1B to ~$81B, and argues leading AI labs could exit 2027 at $1T+ combined revenue run-rate

• Memory Chip Supply: SK Hynix, Kioxia, and SanDisk benefit if long-running AI agents make memory and storage more valuable. Leopold says reinforcement learning and agents make AI chips limited by memory, which is why he viewed Hynix as a $100B company that could become a $1T company

• GPU Rentals: SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, and IREN benefit if AI labs keep renting short-term GPU capacity at higher prices. SALP says an H100 used to earn ~$1-$2/hour, now earns ~$5-$10/hour, and could reach $100s/hour+ if superintelligence demand hits

• Datacenter Power Supply: Bloom Energy benefits if AI datacenters pay more to get power online faster. AI buildout needs more than cheap power, it needs power immediately 

• Robotics: Robotics becomes the next major theme if AI starts doing real-world labor. Leopold says frontier models are starting to beat specialist robotics models, which means the next advancement may come from better AI models

Leopold warns software companies, AI wrappers, chip designers, and even today’s AI winners may lose their moats once AI can replace the engineers, code, IP, and management they are valued on

Stocks to own:

• Anthropic $ANT
• SK Hynix $SKHY
• Kioxia $KXIAY
• SanDisk $SNDK

• IREN $IREN
• Bloom Energy $BE

Stocks to avoid:

• Salesforce $CRM
• Adobe $ADBE
• ServiceNow $NOW

• Synopsys $SNPS
• Arm $ARM
• Nvidia $NVDA
• AMD $AMD

有一些过时的《神鬼寓言 5》系统卡的屏幕截图。在 6 月份《神鬼寓言 5》发布的前两天，我们确实对一些法学硕士研究应用了不可见的保护措施。这是一
celebrity.author: @edwinarbus
celebrity.summary_zh:
个错误，我们于 6 月 10 日逆转了它。这些保护措施现在明确阻止请求或回退，并显示用户可以看到的消息 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback)。

我们确实训练了《神鬼寓言 5.2》使其具有与 Opus 5.5 水平相当的 LLM 研究能力，并在发布时如此表示 (https://anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2)。这会影响能力，但不会默默地破坏工作。

据我们所知，一些报告看起来像是我们所说的模型行为中的“过度谨慎”，即克劳德在长时间运行的任务中过度依赖它为自己制定的规则。这并不是机器学习研究所特有的，我们在没有这些训练变化的模型（包括 Opus 5.5）以及我们自己的工作中也看到了这一点。您可以要求克劳德审查并删除它为自己制定的规则，我们正在努力减少未来模型中的过度谨慎。我们不会故意干扰用户的工作。

我们已直接回复此处要求提供会话 ID 的大量报告，但请分享（运行“/status”）！
celebrity.full_text_en:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback).

We did train Fable 5.2 to have LLM research capabilities at about the level of Opus 5.5, and said so at launch (https://anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2). This impacts capability, but doesn’t silently sabotage work.

As far as we can tell, some reports look like what we call "overcaution" in model behavior, where Claude gets overly attached to rules it makes for itself during long-running tasks. This isn’t specific to ML research, and we see it in models without these training changes (including Opus 5.5) and in our own work too. You can ask Claude to review and remove rules it made for itself, and we're working on reducing overcaution in future models. We’re not in the practice of intentionally disrupting users’ work.

We've replied directly to a bunch of reports on here asking for session IDs but please share (run `/status`)!

celebrity.full_text_en:
I am about 30 pages into the Q3 Situational Awareness letter. The full letter is 160 pages.

All I can say so far is that if Leopold is right about where he sees AI going...the disconnect between market valuations across the AI stack and the level of growth we should expect is one of the largest disconnects we have ever seen in financial markets.

Some of these predictions are quite hard to believe, but I guess that's also the point of his fund. He writes, "Either we or the market will have an extraordinary amount of egg on the face in a year."

Will post deeper thoughts tomorrow after reading through the whole thing, the most interesting insights so far: he thinks the frontier labs will do $1T of ARR by end of 2027, a ChatGPT moment for Robotics will come by late 2027, and that RSI is significantly being discounted by the market which could end up becoming so strong that it could lead to the shutdown of all models by the government.

We are living in one of the craziest times to be an investor.

大的技能。它允许您通过大量人工智能代理来应对复杂的挑战

celebrity.full_text_en:
Google Gemini Neon is the best AI model on planet Earth right now

It's smarter, faster, and more token efficient

The issue is, most people don't know how to use Antigravity, the official Google harness

Here are the most important tips:

🔶 /swarm: this might be the most powerful skill in Antigravity. It allows you to tackle complex challenges with swarms of AI agents

If you have a complex challenge (like architecture planning for instance) that has many different possible solutions, use /swarm

🔶 /grill-me: lots of harnesses have /grill-me, but I like Antigravity's the best. Anytime you are in the beginning stages of building, run this skill. Antigravity will ask you TONS of questions to iron out your plan

🔶 Antigravity on mobile: Antigravity unfortunately has no mobile app. But you can still use it on mobile! Go to settings > Application> remote control. This will generate a link you can send to your phone so you can code as you go

🔶 Antigravity Deep Research: Google just open sourced their official deep research skill, and it's excellent. It's built for Neon and Antigravity. Ask your agent to download the deep-research skill from Google demo lab

🔶 Knowledge work interface: If you're using Neon more for knowledge work, there is a knowledge work UI in the settings to make the overall interface less technical. Try it out!

Feel free to come back to these and let me know any other tips you have!
